sources.access: Measured 2026-10-21. An aggregator is not an open-licence substitute for the publisher (per the standing rule: the aggregator's licence statement may not be the publisher's).

license_evidence: Measured 2026-10-21: knbs.or.ke footer - 'Copyright 2026 (c) Kenya National Bureau of Statistics | All Rights Reserved'. No open-data licence, no terms-of-use page found on the site probed.

Measured 2026-10-21: the only 'data portal' the NSO itself links (kenya.opendataforafrica.org) answers a Cloudflare challenge to anonymous clients, and is a commercial-platform mirror - its terms are not KNBS's, and the publisher's own licence remains unreadable.

The national open-data portal (open.data.go.ke), which historically carried per-dataset licences, no longer resolves, so there is no portal-level licence to read. Per the standing rule, unstated/unreadable terms are not assumed: the licence question is escalated, not decided.

novelty_check.verdict: not run - access and licence vetoes precede novelty work; no candidate dataset reached formulation

rejection_reason: PARK (infrastructure, not a task defect). Three stacked, measured blockers, in order of weight: (1) the national open-data portal open.data.go.ke no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN), so the historical per-dataset licence channel is gone; (2) the NSO's own site is all-rights-reserved with no machine-readable data channel - its data-portals page links out to third parties instead of hosting data; (3) the third-party channels it links are a Cloudflare-walled commercial aggregator (whose terms would not be the publisher's licence anyway) and a static SDG dashboard. Nothing here disqualifies Kenyan statistical products as a task - the publishing machinery just cannot currently carry one. Recorded as an honest empty result for the Africa tick's Kenya probe, with the probes that produced it.
next_action: Unpark question (exact): does any KNBS-published channel offer anonymous bulk/API access with stated licence terms? Concretely, probe in this order: (a) a KNBS microdata/NADA catalogue (IHSN family) - note NADA studies usually require application rather than open bulk, so per-dataset licence terms must be readable; (b) whether Kenya Open Data has a successor domain (search for the portal's successor, then CKAN package_show to read per-dataset licences); (c) sector regulators with their own publishing (Central Bank of Kenya, KRA, NTSA) for a task-shaped series with documented release dates. If all three fail again, the Kenya verdict stays parked and the next Africa tick moves on.
